title: Beyond transversality: structure of Clifford circuits for CSS codes
abstract: We characterize four groups of Clifford circuits for Calderbank--Shor--Steane (CSS) codes that are relevant to fault-tolerant logical operations. First, we show that every code-preserving Clifford circuit is a product of Z-diagonal circuits, composed of S and CZ gates, and their X-basis analogues. Second, we define the two-fold transversal group, generated by depth-one two-local code-preserving circuits, and show that each of its elements can be expressed as a product of layers consisting of either Z-diagonal, X-diagonal, or CNOT gates. As a corollary, every transversal gate is a product of three transversal diagonal circuits; for connected non-self-dual codes, two such circuits suffice.   We further show that every code-preserving automorphism circuit, consisting of single-qubit Clifford gates and permutations, has a normal form comprising a Hadamard layer, a permutation, and two diagonal circuits. We also define a two-fold automorphism group, in which a depth-one two-local circuit may be code-preserving up to a permutation, and show that its logical image can be larger than that of the two-fold transversal group.   For 136 CSS codes, we provide explicit generators and determine the logical image of the two-fold transversal group. We find 78 codes whose full logical Clifford group is generated by two-fold-transversal circuits, including codes of distances 3, 4, 5, 6, 8, and 12, with respective rates $2/5$, $3/4$, $1/9$, $1/5$, $2/5$, and $3/56$. We construct three families of CSS codes from bipartite grids, cut-complements, and quadrics, many of which realize the full logical Clifford group in this way. More generally, the induced logical group can be large even when it is not full logical Clifford group: it has order at least $460\,800$ for the gross code and roughly $10^{26}$ for a clustered-cyclic code.
summary: This paper rigorously characterizes the algebraic structure of Clifford circuits that can preserve the encoding properties of CSS quantum error-correcting codes. By decomposing these circuits into fundamental diagonal and CNOT layers, the authors determine which specific codes allow their logical operations to be generated by relatively simple 'two-fold transversal' gates. This is crucial for designing efficient, fault-tolerant quantum computation protocols.
main_problem: The paper characterizes the structure of Clifford circuits necessary for implementing fault-tolerant logical operations within Calderbank–Shor–Steane (CSS) quantum error-correcting codes.
main_result: It establishes that code-preserving circuits decompose into products of diagonal gates, and it identifies 78 CSS codes whose full logical Clifford group is generated by two-fold transversal circuits.
method: The authors use algebraic methods involving symplectic geometry to analyze the constraints imposed on circuit blocks (Z-diagonal, X-diagonal, CNOT) required for code preservation.
model_or_system: The study focuses on CSS quantum error-correcting codes, which are analyzed using a symplectic formalism where Pauli operators are represented by labels $(x|z)$. The circuits implement logical gates acting on these encoded qubits.
key_observables: The size and structure of the logical Clifford group generated by specific circuit families (e.g., two-fold transversal group).
important_parameters: Code parameters such as distance (3, 4, 5, etc.) and rate ($2/5$, $3/4$, etc.).
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes the relevance of Clifford circuits for fault tolerance and relies on decomposing general code-preserving maps into specific product structures.
figures_summary: Figure 1 illustrates four key Clifford gate families (Z-diagonal, X-diagonal, CNOT, partial duality) for a CSS code. Figure 2 schematically details the generating sets for different gate groups ($\mathcal{N}_{\emptyset}$, $\mathcal{N}_M$, $\mathcal{N}_{2	ext{fold}}$, $\mathcal{N}$).
paper_structure: The paper proceeds by characterizing four distinct families of circuits (code-preserving, transversal, etc.), deriving their normal forms using algebraic constraints, and finally applying these results to enumerate specific CSS codes whose logical group structure is determined.
why_interesting: This work provides deep structural insights into the gate sets required for fault-tolerant quantum computation, which underpins many theoretical models of quantum information processing relevant to AMO physics platforms like trapped ions or superconducting qubits.
